title: Scalar record passed to a loop reader
intent: Use a six-field scalar record as a control for aggregate argument handling without managed payloads.
oracle: The six fields sum to 6n+15. The reader adds that sum and i for i=0..n-1, giving n(6n+15)+n(n-1)/2=(13n^2+29n)/2.
focus: score (line 10) reads six scalar fields in a runtime-length loop; probe constructs and passes the record by value. Any scalar replacement is a valid optimization win.

title: Returned record with a managed list field
intent: Observe allocation and ownership when a factory returns a record containing a runtime-sized list and another function reads its field.
oracle: make_batch stores the integers 1 through n and factor n. score computes n times their sum, n^2(n+1)/2.
focus: make_batch (line 6) fills and returns Batch.items; score (line 13) borrows that field during a loop. The record and its list have different storage lifetimes.

title: Record snapshot kept across managed-field mutation
intent: Measure required snapshot preservation when a mut helper appends to a record's shared list while the original record remains observable.
oracle: The saved record scores n+(n+n+1)=3n+1. The updated record has stamp 2n and appends 1..n, so it scores 4n+1+n(n+1)/2. Print 1000 times the saved score plus the updated score.
focus: probe (line 19) keeps saved alive across extend (line 6), which mutates current.items and current.stamp; both records are read afterwards.

title: Construct and traverse nested lists
intent: Observe ownership transfer of fixed-width inner lists into a runtime-sized outer list, followed by nested borrowing in another function.
oracle: Row i contains i, i+1 and i+2, whose sum is 3i+3. Summing rows i=0..n-1 gives 3n(n+1)/2.
focus: make_rows (line 1) inserts each inner list into rows; score (line 11) traverses both levels. Inner lists have fixed length but escape into a managed container.

title: List of records with dynamic text and list fields
intent: Exercise managed-element insertion, field borrowing and destruction with dynamically produced strings and independently allocated integer lists.
oracle: Entry i has label length 4+digits(n+i), two values, and value sum n+i. Its contribution is 6+digits(n+i)+n+i. For n=4 all labels use one digit, giving 50; for n=11 all use two digits, giving 264.
focus: make_entries (line 6) constructs Entry(label="row:"+str(i+n), values=[i,n]); score (line 13) reads both managed fields. Labels are runtime text rather than only immortal literals.

title: Branch-selected alias mutated beside both originals
intent: Expose alias joins and copy-on-write when one of two lists is selected by a runtime branch, extended, and compared with both original values.
oracle: The original sums are L=2n+1 and R=4n+1. Appending n+2 gives selected sum 3n+3 for even n or 5n+3 for odd n. Print 100L+10R+selected: 1085 and 2808.
focus: choose (line 1) returns an input alias; probe (line 14) appends to the selected value and then reads both originals. The two input sizes exercise different branches.

title: Runtime-selected callback reads a short list
intent: Measure the ownership and allocation boundary of an indirect read-only call on a fixed-length scalar list; permit any valid devirtualization.
oracle: The four values n..n+3 sum to 4n+6. Even n chooses sum_values; odd n chooses double_values, so the outputs are 22 and 2*50=100.
focus: apply (line 15) invokes a function-valued parameter; probe (line 19) selects the callback from runtime parity and constructs the four-element list.

title: Recursive reader of a short scalar list
intent: Observe how an ordinary list borrow crosses recursive calls where the current strict proof remains conservative.
oracle: sum_from visits each index from zero through three once and returns zero at index four. Its result is n+(n+1)+(n+2)+(n+3)=4n+6.
focus: sum_from (line 1) forwards the same list through recursion; probe (line 7) creates a fixed-length list of runtime-dependent values.

title: Returned managed field kept beside its parent
intent: Expose ownership of a list returned from a borrowed record, then mutate the extracted value while retaining the parent snapshot.
oracle: The parent's list sums to 3n+3. Appending n+3 to the extracted list produces sum 4n+6 while the parent remains unchanged. The final checksum is 100(3n+3)+(4n+6)+n=305n+306.
focus: values_of (line 6) returns packet.values; probe (line 17) appends to that returned field and then reads packet.values and packet.id. Inlining the accessor is allowed.

title: Loop-carried list rebuilt by a by-value helper
intent: Measure copies and reference counts when each loop iteration replaces its list with the result of an ordinary by-value batch-append helper, without retaining snapshots.
oracle: Let w=n%3+1. Iteration i appends n+i+j for j=0..w-1. The score adds the final length nw to the sum, giving nw(3n+w)/2. With (n,w)=(4,2) and (11,3), this is 56 and 594.
focus: append_batch (line 1) makes a mutable local from an ordinary input and appends in a runtime-length loop; probe (line 15) carries the returned list into the next call.
